record.what_it_does: Cloud platform for running web scraping and automation Actors, with storage for their results.
record.auth_notes: The REST API uses a personal API token. It is sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' (recommended) or as a ?token= query parameter (less secure). Scoped tokens can be limited to specific resources, but they cannot create or modify Actors. Apify's 'Integrate with Apify' guide lists OAuth 2.0 as a supported way for integrations to authenticate users. Third parties already use OAuth clients registered in Apify Console (Pipedream 'apify-oauth', Activepieces). However, the public docs do not cover how to register an OAuth app, the endpoints or the scopes; they point to integrations@apify.com. The hosted MCP server supports both OAuth and Bearer token.
record.access_notes: The Free plan costs $0, needs no credit card and includes $5 of platform usage each month. Any account can create a personal API token in Console (Settings > API & Integrations). No plan gate on the API is documented. Free-plan Apify Proxy is limited to use within the platform; that limit does not apply to the REST API. Registering a multi-user OAuth app is not self-serve as documented; it appears to go through integrations@apify.com.
record.api_breadth_notes: API v2 sections: Actors, Actor versions, builds, runs, tasks, datasets, key-value stores, request queues, requests and locks, webhooks, webhook dispatches, schedules, store, logs, users, usage and limits, proxy test, and sign/verify. It also has default-storage and last-run endpoint variants. A full OpenAPI schema is available in YAML and JSON; operations number well over 50.
record.mcp_notes: Hosted at https://mcp.apify.com. OAuth is recommended; an 'Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>' header also works. Apify also publishes a local npm package, @apify/actors-mcp-server (GitHub apify/apify-mcp-server).
record.blocker_notes: Personal or scoped API tokens are self-serve on the free plan, which is enough to build now. OAuth 2.0 for integrations exists, but registration is not publicly documented; you would likely need to contact integrations@apify.com for a client ID and secret. Rate limits are generous: 250k requests/min globally and 60 requests/s per resource by default.
